motion_decision.motion_summary: Locked-off static shot of a parked Porsche 911 GT3 and a superyacht in Monaco harbor at sunset. Car, yacht, buildings, mountain, and sky read as static across all 10 contact-sheet frames (0.65s apart); only the harbor water surface shows subtle, continuous rippling reflecting the warm sunset/yacht lights.
motion_decision.reason: Contact-sheet read initially suggested crossfade (ambient-only water ripple, no coherent subject/camera motion). However, per the mandatory empirical verification step, a built crossfade loop segment was inspected and its mid-blend frame (t~4.85s) showed clear ghosting/doubling on the car's license plate, wheel spokes, and the yacht's antenna mast -- meaning the source clip has enough sub-pixel camera micro-jitter/sensor noise between its start and end frames that a direct dissolve does not blend cleanly, even though no frame-to-frame motion was visible across the coarser 10-frame contact sheet. Switched to reverse (ping-pong with speed ramp) after this empirical failure, per agents/long_form/3.2_animator.md's verification step -- both loop points become exact (identical frame at the cut) rather than blended, which eliminates the ghosting regardless of the micro-jitter.

queue.animation_note: Initial crossfade attempt (min(2.0,max(0.6,5.875*0.12))=0.705s blend) FAILED empirical mid-blend-frame verification -- visible ghosting/doubling on license plate, wheels, and yacht mast at t~4.85s despite a clean-looking 10-frame contact sheet. Rebuilt with method=reverse instead: last 1.5s of the 5.875s clip decelerated via the standard 5-step setpts ramp (1.0/1.2/1.45/1.75/2.2x), reversed half built from that same ramped clip so both sides of the cut ease symmetrically.
